thread:
jamal: Quick heads up — the rerank endpoint semantics are drifting across PRs. Current protos differ on whether we return per-candidate metadata (model, raw_score, norm_score) vs a compact array. Need a short decision before the next release.

selene: Can you paste the two shapes?

jamal: Sure — current live shape: 
```json
{"candidates": [
  {"id": "c1", "score": 0.83},
  {"id": "c2", "score": 0.79}
]}
```
Proposed envelope: 
```json
{"items": [
  {"id": "c1", "score": 830, "normalized_score": 0.83, "model": "scorer-v2", "units": 12},
  {"id": "c2", "score": 790, "normalized_score": 0.79, "model": "scorer-v2", "units": 11}
], "meta": {"scorer_model": "scorer-v2", "billing_units": 23}}
```

li: My vote is envelope. We need model attribution for routing/telemetry and units to charge correctly. Compact arrays break that.

tony: 👍 on metadata but worried about payload size for large candidate sets (N=200). Also need clarity on score encoding: ints (0-1000) or floats? Integers give stable transport but lose precision.

selene: For size, we can make per-candidate fields optional unless requested. Maybe add query param `include_candidate_meta=true`. Default stays compact for small snippets.

rachel: Telemetry perspective: we need per-candidate latency histograms and cache_hit flags. If we don't return model, it's hard to trace which scorer produced the value in multi-model rollouts. Also need tags for KV cache hits so we can measure effective batching improvements.

jamal: Agreed. Proposal: default compact response (id+score) for backward compat. New param `format=envelope` for full metadata. Add `scoring_model` at top-level and `model` per item when heterogeneous scoring used. Account units at request-level and optional per-item `units`.

tony: OK but accounting rules? Bill per-candidate? Per-request max of top-k? We have Dedicated customers who expect predictable commits.

li: We should decouple billing units from returned `units` to support policy. Use internal `compute_units` for billing and optional `estimated_units` for visibility. Billing always derives from routing decision (which model was executed and how many candidates).

selene: That sounds sane. Also propose a compatibility mode: accept legacy flat arrays and return a header `X-Rerank-Format: legacy|envelope`. That helps SDKs detect when to parse.

rachel: Console/rollouts UX: we should allow canary by scorer variant per route (e.g., 5% scorer-v2, 95% scorer-v1) and show per-variant quality delta on dashboard (precision@k, latency, cost). Can we get model attribution in eval flows?

jamal: Yes — we can emit per-variant metrics to telemetry and surface on Console. Need a minimal telemetry schema: `route`, `scorer_variant`, `candidate_count`, `topk_precision`, `request_units`, `per_candidate_latency_ms`.

tony: One more: rate limits and quotas. If we bill per-candidate, we need new quota units and enforcement at routing layer to prevent heavy scorers from exhausting pool. Suggest `scorer_units` quota and fallback policy to lighter model when quota low.

li: Fallback policy should be policy-driven: `fallback=model:scorer-lite` or `fallback=truncate:k` (only rerank top-k with heavy scorer). Make default safe (truncate).

selene: Implementation note: add `output_format` param (compact|envelope), `include_candidate_meta` bool, `scoring_model_hint` to pin model affinity, and server-side header `X-Scorer-Selection` for debugging.

jamal: Can someone draft a tiny API PR with shapes and header list? I can wire telemetry after we agree.

rachel: I'll sketch dashboard cards for per-variant cost/latency/Q. Will add a mock to the Console tickets.

tony: deployment-wise, we should canary the envelope format change behind a flag in the SDK so old clients don't break.

deploy-bot: Reminder: planned canary window for scorer-v2 rollout tomorrow 09:00-11:00 UTC. Auto-rollback on error rate spike > 2x baseline or latency p95 > 2s. :robot_face:

jamal: Perfect. Thanks all — I'll open the PR and link it here. :thumbsup:
